newsitem.title: USA: Crown Cork stock sinks, earnings fall short.
newsitem.headline: Crown Cork stock sinks, earnings fall short.

text.p: Shares of packaging manufacturer Crown Cork & Seal Co Inc slid around 11 percent after the company disappointed Wall Street by posting second quarter earnings which were below analysts' expectations.

Crown Cork reported second quarter earnings of $0.94 per diluted share versus $0.74 per share in the year-ago quarter and a consensus estimate of about $1.04 per share. Excluding one-time gains for asset sales, analysts said Crown Cork's earnings were between $0.84 and $0.87 per share.
The stock shed 5-7/8 to 50-1/2 in brisk trade.
"They missed the numbers big time and analysts are bringing down their estimates," Cornelius Thornton, an analyst at Goldman Sachs, said.
Thornton, who rates the shares a market outperform, said he cut his 1997 earnings estimate to $2.85 per share from $3.00 and moved his 1998 estimate to $3.50 from $3.60 a share.
Daniel Khoshaba, an analyst at Salomon Brothers who rates Crown a buy, lowered his 1997 estimate to $2.45 per share from $3.40 and his 1998 estimate to $3.35 per share from $4.50.

The company said its second quarter net sales were marginally lower than the year-ago second quarter's because of the dollar's strength against other European currencies, operations divested after the second quarter of 1996 and the pass-through of lower raw material costs to customers.
But Khoshaba said Crown Cork's earnings were bound to be uneven, as the company worked on integrating its French unit CarnaudMetalbox, acquired last year.
"Crown Cork is in the process of merging two large companies, so its earnings are bound to be lumpy," he said.
Thornton said foreign exchange only hurt Crown Cork about $0.04 per share in the second quarter.
